page: Microsoft Azure E64ps_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the arm64 architecture, powered by 64 dedicated physical cores of the Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. Featuring a single thread per core, the instance provides 128 MB of L3 cache alongside 512 GB of system memory, matching a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio (8 GB per core). As an Epsv6 series member running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system does not bundle any local ephemeral storage or hardware GPUs, directing storage operations entirely to external network-attached storage.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional multi-threaded and memory-intensive throughput. The server achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng tests and Geekbench multi-core evaluation, alongside strong results in clang compilation benchmarks and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidth both reach the top 10% bracket at 465.5 GB/s and 203.88 GB/s, respectively. Conversely, single-core execution metrics across Geekbench and stress-ng fall into the average range, underscoring that raw throughput stems from parallelism across dedicated cores rather than peak single-thread frequency.

The 64-core dedicated ARM design offers high compute density and energy efficiency, eliminating hyper-threading performance jitter while maintaining predictable memory throughput across all 512 GB. However, workloads requiring local scratch disks or hardware accelerators face architectural tradeoffs due to the absence of onboard NVMe storage and GPUs.

Azure E64ps_v6 is well suited for memory-bound applications including large in-memory key-value stores such as Redis, large relational and NoSQL database deployments, parallel compilation pipelines, and memory-intensive enterprise software.
description: Microsoft Azure E64ps_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by 64 dedicated physical ARM Neoverse-N2 cores clocked at 3.4 GHz. Operating on a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the instance integrates 512 GB of RAM alongside 128 MB of L3 cache on an arm64 architecture. Hardware accelerators and local disk storage are omitted, requiring remote disk infrastructure. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded compute, high-throughput clang software compilation, and uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 465 GB/s for reads and 203 GB/s for writes. Single-core processing speeds remain moderate, confirming that performance gains are driven by parallel resource distribution rather than single-thread clock rates. The dedicated core model avoids noisy-neighbor contention across virtual threads, delivering consistent resource allocation. Azure E64ps_v6 is specifically matched for in-memory databases, large caching layers such as Redis, distributed analytics, and large-scale parallel software build pipelines.
